set_aside.question: What happens if Portal publication succeeds but recording the publication id fails or the calling flow stops between those operations?
options: Use an idempotency key understood by the Portal
Persist a recoverable transaction in the caller
Provide an explicit owner-assisted reconciliation flow
Retry publication and infer the result from Portal data
set_aside.default_guess: Persist an operation id before publishing and require idempotent publication or an explicit reconciliation path before retrying.

witness.initial: A chosen photo is placed but has no publication mark.
events: The calling flow publishes it successfully.
The flow crashes before recording the Portal photo id.
The owner retries after the photo has been shown.
outcomes: A retry republishes, conflicts or creates a duplicate without knowing the original id.
The original Portal id is reconciled and recorded without another publication.

set_aside.subject: concurrent delivery
set_aside.text: A failed photo does not stop the others.
set_aside.question: Can two delivery flows act on the same project or content concurrently, and what prevents duplicate Portal publication before either flow records its result?
options: Serialize delivery per project
Claim each content identity atomically
Rely on Portal idempotency
set_aside.default_guess: Atomically claim each project-and-content identity before publication and return the first completed result to later callers.

witness.initial: The same ready photo appears in two workplace sessions.
events: Two owner actions start nearly simultaneously.
Both flows place the idempotent source.
Both publish before either records a Portal id.
outcomes: Two hidden Portal photos are created.
Only one publication occurs and both flows resolve to it.

set_aside.subject: hide superseded photo
set_aside.text: The earlier delivery stays in the Portal until the owner hides it.
set_aside.question: What concrete action lets the owner identify and hide a superseded photo, and what are its observable success and failure outcomes?
options: Use an existing named Portal action outside this service
Add a workplace action that calls the Portal
Leave hiding as a manual undocumented Portal procedure
set_aside.default_guess: Name the existing Portal hide action and specify that the owner performs it directly, with Portal-confirmed visibility as the result.

set_aside.subject: old-date repair
set_aside.text: The agent repairs one project at a time, with a backup and the owner's permission for that project.
set_aside.question: What concrete repair action is performed, what input and backup are used, what observable result proves success, and what failures leave the project unchanged or recoverable?
options: Define a separate backed-up migration action with verification and rollback
Treat repair as a manual database procedure
Have the Portal expose a supported repair operation
set_aside.default_guess: Define a per-project migration that records permission, creates a restorable backup, previews changes, applies them transactionally and verifies every repaired date.

set_aside.subject: date-offset delivery gate
set_aside.text: If a date still carries an offset, it stops, places and publishes nothing, and tells the owner.
set_aside.question: Which project's photos are checked, what representation counts as carrying an offset, and what exact result or reason is reported?
options: Block if any existing Portal photo for the project has a non-UTC or offset-bearing stored value
Check only photos selected for this delivery
Check only legacy photos identified by the repair process
set_aside.default_guess: Check all existing Portal photos in the target project and return the offending Portal photo ids before any placement.

witness.initial: A project has one old Portal photo with +02:00 and one newly selected source photo.
events: The owner starts delivery.
One implementation checks only the selected source.
Another checks every existing Portal photo in the project.
outcomes: The new photo is placed and published.
The entire delivery stops before placement.

set_aside.subject: prepared image encoding
set_aside.text: A stored image carries no EXIF, GPS, XMP or comment, is upright and is at most 2000 px on its longest side.
set_aside.question: What output format, color handling, resize rule, animation handling, quality and metadata-stripping verification define the prepared image?
options: Specify a canonical deterministic image profile
Preserve the source format where possible
Let the image library choose defaults
set_aside.default_guess: Specify a canonical sRGB still-image profile, deterministic orientation and resize behavior, fixed encoding quality, and verified removal of all nonessential metadata.

witness.initial: A selected wide-gamut animated image has an EXIF orientation and is 3000 pixels wide.
events: Two implementations prepare it using different image-library defaults.
outcomes: It becomes a single-frame sRGB JPEG with fixed quality.
It remains animated or uses another format, color conversion and quality while still satisfying the stated limits.

set_aside.subject: file stability
set_aside.text: A file is taken only after it has been unchanged for two minutes
set_aside.question: Which observed attributes establish 'unchanged', when does the interval start or reset, and how are clock changes and edits during reading handled?
options: Require unchanged size, mtime and content identity over two observations
Use modification time age only
Use filesystem notifications followed by a quiet interval
set_aside.default_guess: Track size and high-resolution mtime across observations for two minutes, then snapshot and hash the bytes before placement.

witness.initial: A file's contents are replaced while its size and modification time are preserved.
events: Two minutes pass after the original observation.
One implementation uses size and mtime.
Another verifies content identity.
outcomes: The replacement is treated as the stable scanned photo.
The change is detected and the stability interval restarts.

set_aside.subject: ignored filenames
set_aside.text: Syncthing's temporary files and hidden names, which include the phone's `.trashed-` files, are ignored.
set_aside.question: What exact filename and path rules identify hidden names and Syncthing temporary files at every folder depth?
options: Define explicit component-level patterns
Ignore every path component beginning with a dot
Delegate classification to Syncthing conventions
set_aside.default_guess: Ignore any path with a dot-prefixed component and an explicit versioned set of Syncthing temporary-name patterns.

set_aside.unit: 00_product.md:Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18): Accepted from the experiment (owner, 2026-11-18)
set_aside.subject: photo date extraction
set_aside.text: The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset.
set_aside.question: Which camera field wins, how is a camera time without timezone converted to UTC, and what exact offset-free representation is sent?
options: Use a specified EXIF field plus explicit offset fields, rejecting timezone-less camera dates
Apply a configured project timezone to timezone-less camera dates
Treat timezone-less camera dates as already UTC
set_aside.default_guess: Use a documented field precedence, apply an embedded offset when present, otherwise apply a confirmed project timezone, then serialize a defined UTC value.

witness.initial: A photo has DateTimeOriginal 2026-07-01 12:00 with no offset, from a camera used in Madrid.
events: The file is delivered during summer time.
One implementation treats the value as UTC.
Another interprets it in Europe/Madrid and converts it to UTC.
outcomes: The Portal receives 12:00 UTC.
The Portal receives 10:00 UTC.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the photo date

set_aside.subject: service deployment
set_aside.text: Where does the service run and how does the kernel reach it?
set_aside.question: What host, process/container boundary, lifecycle, filesystem mounts and network exposure run the service on the VPS?
options: Run it as a host service with restricted filesystem access
Run it in a container with explicit Syncthing and Portal-store mounts
Run it inside the kernel process
set_aside.default_guess: Run it as a separate container or system service with read-only Syncthing mounts and the minimum required write access to the Portal store.

set_aside.subject: kernel authentication
set_aside.text: the kernel needs an HTTPS route and its own credential for the service
set_aside.question: Who issues, stores, rotates and revokes the credential; how is the kernel authenticated and authorized; and is the route exposed beyond the VPS?
options: Use mutually authenticated TLS on a private network
Use a scoped bearer credential over a private HTTPS route
Expose public HTTPS with a scoped credential and network controls
set_aside.default_guess: Use a private HTTPS route with a narrowly scoped rotatable credential stored by the kernel and accepted only from the intended network boundary.

witness.initial: The service is running on the VPS and can read project folders and write the Portal store.
events: An untrusted process obtains network reachability to the service.
One implementation relies only on route secrecy.
Another requires and validates a scoped kernel credential.
outcomes: The process can request placements or scans.
The process is refused without the kernel identity.
